summary: Iteration 2 testing of Belt-Sentinel: 11 pytest cases against the new Supabase-backed endpoints (/api/sensors, /api/history/joint, /api/history/all-joints, /api/joint/passport, /api/admin/seed) plus simulator/LLM regression, and a Playwright pass over the unauthenticated auth flow (ProtectedRoute redirects, /login + /signup structure, bad-credential handling). Backend 9/11 passed; both failures trace to one root cause: Supabase PostgREST caps every response at 1000 rows, so the 60D/90D history windows are truncated. Frontend auth: 8/8 checks passed. Authenticated dashboard/HistoricalTrend/Sidebar UI was NOT tested (no confirmed Supabase test user, per instructions in /app/memory/test_credentials.md).

critical.issue: Returns exactly 1000 points per joint for days=45,60,75,90 (identical payloads). Supabase PostgREST enforces a hard db-max-rows=1000 cap, so the code's limit=1200 is silently ignored. Result: the 30/60/90-day toggle in HistoricalTrend is a no-op beyond ~40 days - 60D and 90D render the exact same chart. Verified counts: 30d=794, 45d=1000, 60d=1000, 75d=1000, 90d=1000.

Because order=timestamp.asc is combined with the 1000-row cap, the rows returned are the OLDEST 1000 in the window and the NEWEST data is dropped. For a 90-day window the series ends 2026-07-30 while the latest row in joint_history is 2026-09-04 (today is 2026-09-01) - the chart is missing the most recent ~5 weeks, including all recent degradation. passport.latest correctly shows 2026-09-04 but trend_90d stops at 2026-07-30, so the passport is internally inconsistent.

minor.issue: trend_90d returned exactly 1000 rows (test expected >1000). Same 1000-row cap; limit=2500 in code is ineffective.

No try/except around sb.select(). A SupabaseError (RLS change, network blip, 4xx from PostgREST) propagates as an unhandled 500 with a stack trace instead of a 502/503 with a meaningful message. No graceful degradation for the frontend.
days/joint_id are unvalidated (no Pydantic/Query constraints): days=-5 or days=99999 and arbitrary joint_id strings are accepted and return 200 with an empty rows array rather than 400/404.

integration_issues.issue: Consequence of the backend 1000-row cap: clicking 60D and 90D produces an identical chart, and both end ~5 weeks before 'now'. The 'N points shown' footer will read the same value for 60D and 90D. Could not be visually confirmed (login required), but is deterministic from the API responses.

issues: The 'PS-26008 · CLASSIFIED' badge uses #5A6063 on #121416 at 9px - contrast ratio is well below WCAG AA and is effectively illegible in the screenshot.
The 'EMAIL' / 'PASSWORD' field labels (#757575 at 10px) are also low-contrast against #1A1C1E.

action_items: Fix the 1000-row PostgREST cap: either paginate with the Range header / offset loop in supabase_client.select() until all rows are fetched, or (preferred for chart payload size) do server-side downsampling via a Postgres RPC/view that buckets joint_history to N points per window.
Until pagination exists, switch history queries to order=timestamp.desc + limit, then reverse in Python, so the MOST RECENT data is always shown instead of the oldest.
Ensure 60D and 90D produce visibly different series (assert point counts differ) before demoing the toggle.
Wrap sb.select() calls in try/except SupabaseError and return 502/503 with a clear message so the frontend can show trend-error instead of a raw 500.
Add Query(ge=1, le=365) validation on `days` and validate joint_id against the J1-J4 set.

Create a confirmed Supabase test user (turn off 'Confirm email' or SQL-confirm one) and update /app/memory/test_credentials.md so the authenticated dashboard, HistoricalTrend and Sidebar UI can actually be tested.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: limit=1200/2500/5000 passed to PostgREST is a false sense of safety - Supabase silently truncates at 1000. Any query expected to exceed 1000 rows must paginate via Range/offset or aggregate server-side.
server.py history_all(): the per-joint sequential loop issues 4 serial HTTP round-trips to Supabase; use asyncio.gather to cut latency by ~4x (30d call currently ~2-4s).

supabase_client.py: module-level SUPABASE_URL/SUPABASE_KEY are snapshotted at import time while _url()/_key() read lazily - two sources of truth. Drop the module attributes and have the seed script call the functions.

server.py: no downsampling on the server side - /api/joint/passport ships up to 1000 full rows and HistoricalTrend re-downsamples client-side (stride math in useMemo). Move the stride to the API to shrink payloads.

Supabase anon key with insert policy is exposed to the browser AND used by /api/admin/seed with no auth; POST /api/admin/seed is publicly callable and can be forced (force=true) by anyone. Gate it behind a secret/header.

rca_of_the_issue: Root cause of both backend failures is a single defect: Supabase/PostgREST applies a server-side db-max-rows limit of 1000 to every REST response. supabase_client.select() passes `limit` as a PostgREST query param, which can only lower - never raise - that ceiling, so limit=1200 (history/all-joints), limit=2500 (passport trend) and limit=5000 (history/joint) all resolve to 1000. Reproduction: GET /api/history/all-joints?days=45|60|75|90 -> every joint returns exactly 1000 points with identical first/last timestamps (2026-06-18T11:20Z -> 2026-07-30T02:20Z), while GET /api/joint/passport reports latest.timestamp=2026-09-04T13:20Z. Because the query is ordered timestamp.asc, truncation removes the newest data, not the oldest. Mitigation: paginate with the HTTP Range header (Range: 0-999, 1000-1999, ...) inside select(), or expose a Postgres RPC that time-buckets joint_history and returns <=1000 aggregated points per window; as an immediate stopgap, query timestamp.desc and reverse client-side so at least the latest 1000 points are shown.
